description: Rename a web tracking key, replace its allowed origins or app IDs, or revoke it. `allowedOrigins` and `allowedAppIds` each REPLACE the whole list rather than appending, so include the entries you want to keep. Revoking with isActive: false stops events within about a minute while preserving the key value, so the customer can still find and remove the matching snippet from their site; use delete_web_tracking_key only once the snippet is gone.

allowedAppIds.description: Replacement list of iOS bundle IDs and Android package names. The key becomes unrestricted when both this and allowedOrigins are empty. Adding app IDs to a key with no origins makes it app-only: a website already using it stops sending events, so add the site's origins too or create a separate key for the app.

allowedOrigins.description: Replacement allowed-origins list. The key becomes unrestricted when both this and allowedAppIds are empty.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

id.description: Web tracking key ID from list_web_tracking_keys.

isActive.description: Set false to revoke the key, true to re-enable a revoked one.

name: update_web_tracking_key

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `update_web_tracking_key` MCP tool.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
